one_line_contribution: A measurement paper that defines a substitution ratio S quantifying how much of an ExpeL-style procedural memory bank's reported gain survives once a reflective prompt optimizer (GEPA) is given exactly the same training episodes, plus a frozen 'compiled bank' instruction arm (I0xM2) testing whether inference-time retrieval can be deleted entirely.
closest_prior_work: The proposal treats MemDelta (2606.29914) as the main threat, but MemDelta only threatens the framing, and the proposal is right that it audits a different confound. The sharper threat is the prompt-optimization literature's own instruction-vs-demonstration ablations: MIPRO/MIPROv2 and DSPy explicitly decompose a prompt into instructions plus bootstrapped demonstrations and report ablations in which an optimized instruction absorbs much of the value of selected demonstrations, and GEPA's headline result is that reflective instruction evolution beats demonstration-heavy and RL baselines. An ExpeL bank served at top-k=7 is mechanically retrieved demonstrations plus distilled insights, so 'optimized instruction substitutes for retrieved demonstrations' is close to a known finding in the optimizer literature re-dressed in memory clothing. This does not fully kill novelty (the matched-training-episode constraint, the compiled-static instrument, and the residual-gain moderator analysis are not in MIPRO/GEPA), but the paper must confront it and currently does not mention it at all. The unverified TERMS-Bench, flagged by a prior reviewer as a GEPA-based substitution test for a non-prompt intervention, would be a direct precedent for the logical move if it exists.
strongest_objection: The primary endpoint S is confounded with co-adaptation, and the authors cut the one arm that would resolve it. The numerator acc(I1xM1) - acc(I1xM0) measures what memory adds on top of an instruction GEPA optimized in an explicitly memory-free context (I1 'never sees the bank', advertised as a feature so B-dup can reuse I1). An instruction hill-climbed for 300 rollouts with no retrieved block in context will encode a procedure that presumes that context is absent and can conflict with an injected 7-item block; the research track's own prior results say injection volume is the causal lever for memory harm, with a full 7-item bank fixing zero items and breaking six to seven. The likely outcome is acc(I1xM1) <= acc(I1xM0), giving S >= 1, which the proposal never discusses even though it predicts S with a bootstrap CI as if bounded. A high S is then equally well explained by 'the optimized instruction crowds out or conflicts with injected memory' as by 'the information is substitutable' - different mechanisms with opposite engineering implications. Since the contribution is mechanistic, this rival explanation is fatal as designed, and cutting I2 because it 'tests co-adaptation, not substitution' inverts the logic: co-adaptation is exactly the rival hypothesis that must be excluded before substitution can be claimed. Secondary form of the same flaw: the fairness constraint is matched training episodes, but GEPA additionally receives 300 rollouts of scored feedback and Pareto selection on a validation set while the bank is one-shot distilled with no reward signal, so a high S may only show that search with feedback beats no search. Third, the precheck gate lets a failing bank be 'enriched (more training episodes, better distillation) until it passes' a 10-point threshold on a 150-instance dev split - a researcher-degrees-of-freedom loop that both breaks the matched-episode constraint (GEPA is not re-run on the enlarged split) and inflates the denominator of S, biasing the headline toward the hypothesis in a paper whose entire selling point is measurement rigor.
what_would_fix_it: Restore I2 as load-bearing in two forms: GEPA optimized with the retrieved block in context, and at minimum a memory-aware hand-written instruction crossed with M1; report S under memory-blind and memory-aware instructions and treat the gap as evidence for crowd-out rather than substitution. Add a search-matched memory arm (a bank pruned or item-selected against validation reward under the same 300-rollout budget) so the comparison is container-vs-container rather than search-vs-no-search. Delete the 'enrich until it passes' loop or freeze the enrichment protocol before any dev delta is inspected, and re-run GEPA on the enlarged split so matched episodes survive. Demote S to secondary and make the two raw paired deltas with fix/break decompositions primary, since a ratio with a selected denominator and a sign-flipping numerator has a sampling distribution a cluster bootstrap will not rescue; state what S > 1 and S < 0 mean. Grade the positive control: B-dup sets the instrument's sensitivity at a signal level where the answer is essentially inside the retrieved item, far above any realistic procedural bank, so passing it does not license the claim that a null on E1/E2 is a finding rather than a power failure - add weakened tiers (paraphrase-only, same-schema-different-entity) and show detection survives as signal degrades.
missing_baseline: I2, the instruction optimized with memory in context (and its cheap proxy, a memory-aware I0 crossed with M1), which the proposal explicitly cuts; without it S cannot separate substitution from an optimized instruction failing to use a block it was never optimized against. Same family: a memory arm optimized under the same feedback and rollout budget GEPA gets (validation-based bank pruning or item selection) - the iso-cost curve only grows the bank at fixed retrieval, which is not search-matched. Also missing for prediction 3: a retrieval-ceiling control (gold-item or oracle top-k), since I0xM2 tying I0xM1 is trivially explained by weak top-k=7 dense retrieval rather than by compilation being sufficient, and the shuffled-bank sanity check does not show retrieval is near its ceiling.
preprint_collision: Above average, and the honest retraction of five previously cited papers the current search could not return is a genuine credit. It correctly identifies MemDelta as a partial framing collision, correctly argues it is not a claim collision, and correctly declines to lean on EvoClinician. It is thin in three specific ways. First, it reports no search procedure: no queries, no date window, no venues, only 'the current literature search', so coverage cannot be judged - for a proposal whose novelty rests on 'nobody has used an optimizer as the control for memory', that is not adequate evidence of absence. Second, it never searches the side most likely to have scooped it: MIPRO/MIPROv2, DSPy, GEPA and successors routinely ablate optimized instructions against bootstrapped or selected demonstrations, which is the same substitution question one level up, and the check does not mention them. Third, it concedes it could not sweep OpenReview 2026 and could not verify TERMS-Bench, the item a prior reviewer named as the closest structural precedent for exactly the logical move claimed as novel, yet still claims the move is new. I found no preprint that already reports this specific substitution ratio with matched training episodes plus a compiled-static arm, so the claim does not appear scooped outright, but its novelty rests on an unaudited search.
